conceptZh: 巨型玩具兔的超級大耳朵聽到聲音嚇一大跳，雙耳直立展開並組合成傳統漢字「耳」，玩具身體滑出鏡頭外。
object: a cheerful mechanical toy bunny robot with absurdly giant oversized ears
morph: the giant ears spring straight up in surprise, unfolding and snapping into rigid strokes that form the exact Traditional Chinese glyph 耳
creativeAngle: 結合家長意見「超級大耳朵」，以機械玩具兔耳朵過大、聽到聲音嚇一跳的滑稽喜劇動作，自然演變成「耳」字結構。
promptEn: An 8-second 3D animated educational video in a bright, clean aesthetic. Set against a light-cream studio backdrop, a cheerful mechanical toy bunny robot with absurdly giant oversized ears stands in the center. At 0 to 2 seconds, a funny squeak sounds off-screen, making the bunny's giant ears pop straight up in dramatic comic surprise. From 2 to 5 seconds, the oversized ears unfold and snap smoothly into rigid, saturated golden-yellow strokes—two outer vertical columns and four horizontal crossbars—forming the exact Traditional Chinese character "耳". The toy bunny's body comically drops downward out of frame, leaving the target glyph perfectly centered and uncropped, filling 70% of frame height. From 5 to 8 seconds, the scene maintains a clean 3-second static hold on the clear glyph "耳". Warm off-screen Taiwanese Mandarin narration speaks: "耳、耳、耳朵". No subtitles, no on-screen text other than the target glyph, and no visual clutter.

conceptZh: 「耳」字戴著機械玩具耳朵，一顆小鈴鐺只發出細細的吱聲，耳朵卻誇張地展開成巨大收音碟。
object: A solid teal 耳 glyph with detachable mechanical listening ears and a miniature wind-up bell.
morph: The correctly formed glyph stays unchanged; separate toy ears unfold into oversized listening dishes, then retract completely behind it.
creativeAngle: 用小聲音配超大耳朵的尺寸反差製造笑點；字形從頭保持完整，避免耳朵變筆畫造成結構混淆。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated toy-comedy clip in a softly lit peach studio. Center one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph, 耳, in saturated solid teal, occupying about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use a clean, standard Traditional Chinese typeface, preserving its exact stroke lengths and intersections throughout. The glyph is a rigid toy sculpture, viewed straight on with a locked camera. Separate orange mechanical toy ears sit beside it on short hinged arms, visibly distinct from the teal strokes. A miniature wind-up bell stands in the lower-right margin. At 0.0–1.4 seconds, the bell proudly winds its little crank and rocks backward in preparation for an impressive ring; the listening ears incline toward it. At 1.4–2.0 seconds, its clapper swings, but produces only a tiny, soft rubber squeak. After a brief anticipation pause, at 2.2–3.4 seconds both mechanical ears unfold like toy satellite dishes to absurdly oversized proportions, eagerly trying to hear that ridiculously small sound. Keep the entire assembly inside the frame and the glyph fully exposed. At 3.4–4.4 seconds, the ears fold neatly away behind the sculpture while the bell rolls out of view. From 4.4–8.0 seconds, hold the single finished 耳 completely still, centered and unobstructed against the empty peach background. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly “耳、耳、耳朵”: first 耳 at approximately 0.4 seconds, second 耳 at 3.6 seconds, and 耳朵 at 5.5 seconds during the clear final hold. Allow natural pauses and stop after the word. Keep the squeak gentle and separate from the narration; use no background music. Only 耳 appears as visible text, with no vocabulary captions, subtitles, additional lettering, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 科學家老鼠用耳朵聽冒泡聲，泡沫卻替牠戴上巨大耳罩；牠轉動耳朵倒回泡沫，終於聽見小小的啵聲。
object: An original bespectacled cartoon lab mouse and one compact twin-beaker bubbling apparatus beside a solid teal 耳 sculpture.
morph: The glyph stays rigid and correctly formed throughout. Overflowing foam briefly becomes oversized earmuffs on the mouse, then slides back into the beakers.
creativeAngle: 改用老鼠聽實驗聲的失誤呈現耳朵功能：想聽清楚，卻被泡沫耳罩堵住。笑點發生在字旁，避免把耳朵硬拆成筆畫，完整字形從頭保持清楚。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animated comedy with a locked frontal camera and a bright buttercream background. A single correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 耳 stands centered as a flat, saturated teal sculpture, filling approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. Use an accurate standard Traditional Chinese textbook glyph; preserve every stroke, intersection, and open space throughout. In the lower-right margin, stage an original bespectacled cartoon lab mouse with enormous round ears, a tiny lavender lab coat, and an excessively confident scientific manner. Its only accompanying prop is one compact apparatus holding two joined bubbling beakers. Keep the mouse and apparatus distinctly beside the glyph, never overlapping its strokes. All characters and objects have clearly stylized animated forms.

At the opening, the mouse proudly adjusts its glasses and bends one ear toward the gently bubbling beakers. By 1.5 seconds, it leans closer, eagerly trying to catch the faint sound. After a tiny anticipation pause, both beakers fizz over at 2.0 seconds: two soft foam domes rise directly onto its ears, becoming absurdly oversized fluffy earmuffs. The mouse freezes with wide eyes, then taps one muff with a baffled expression; it can no longer hear the bubbling. At 2.8 seconds, it tilts its head and swivels its broad ears downward, neatly pouring both foam caps back into the beakers. A single quiet bubble pops at 3.3 seconds. Its newly uncovered ear perks toward the sound, and the mouse beams with scientific satisfaction. It then wheels the little apparatus out through the right edge, fully exiting by 4.7 seconds. Hold the isolated, centered, uncropped 耳 completely still from 4.7 through 8.0 seconds, with empty margins and no remaining foam.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly “耳、耳、耳朵”. Speak the first 耳 around 0.3 seconds, the second around 1.2 seconds after a short pause, and 耳朵 around 5.5 seconds during the unobstructed final hold. Use natural, unhurried pronunciation and stop after the word. Keep the gentle fizz and soft bubble pop below the narration; use no music. The vocabulary is audio only. The sole visible text is 耳, with no subtitles, labels, additional lettering, logos, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects.
